$comment: Demo/presentation metadata for James. Not snapshot fields — see sarah.json.

partial.via: day 6, hrv_ms null so rule 1.1 is unevaluable

in_balance.via: day 0 (a true calm day, F2) and day 1 (THE JAMES GAP, F5)

$james_gap_note: Day 1 is the whole point of this persona. His RHR sits 26% above baseline, his steps have collapsed, and the app still says 'in balance today' — because rule 1.3 is dual-gated on temperature AND RHR, and with no temperature rise it evaluates cleanly to FALSE. There are no warnings and no unevaluable rows, so nothing in the Decision distinguishes that day from a genuinely calm one. Pinned by F5, and by F5b as a strict xfail that flips the day candidate rule 1.4 is approved. The scenario labels the day so a reviewer sees the defect in the demo rather than only in a Python test.
$no_cycle_note: James has no cycle data, which makes rules 2.1-2.4 UNEVALUABLE every single day — identically to a subject whose cycle data merely failed to sync. That is why app-states.json narrows the 'partial' predicate to Layer 1: counting all layers would make James permanently 'partial' and erase in_balance, taking F2 and F5 out of the demo.
